title: PIMDup: An Optimized Deduplication Design on a Real Processing-in-Memory System
problem: Data deduplication requires scanning entire datasets during chunking, causing excessive data movement between memory and compute. Conventional architectures (GPUs, FPGAs) suffer from von Neumann bottlenecks; processing-in-memory (PIM) systems face unique constraints including restricted inter-DPU sharing and high DPU-CPU communication overhead.
motivation: Deduplication enhances storage efficiency but data movement and memory hierarchy traversals severely limit performance; PIM architecture (UPMEM DPU) offers near-data processing but requires specialized optimization.
method: PIMDup optimizes deduplication on UPMEM DPUs through efficient parallelization, DPU-friendly chunking techniques that avoid multiplication, and reduced data transfer volumes between DPU and CPU, maintaining 100% result consistency.
key_novelty: First deduplication system co-designed for PIM constraints: elimination of inter-DPU sharing limits through parallelization and DPU-friendly chunking without native multiplication.
contributions: DPU-optimized chunking algorithm avoiding multiplication operations
Efficient parallelization strategy for deduplication on PIM
1.67x speedup over CPU-based systems with 100% accuracy preservation
limitations: Optimization specific to UPMEM DPU architecture; generalization to other PIM systems not discussed.
primary_theme: PIM-optimized deduplication with reduced data movement
